minor.issue: On mail-provider failure the endpoint returns HTTP 502. The Cloudflare/ingress edge REPLACES the origin body with its own English HTML error page, so the German detail ('Mailversand ist fehlgeschlagen. Der Handoff wurde nicht verändert.') never reaches the browser. Verified: origin (localhost:8001) returns the correct JSON detail; via the public URL only the CF page arrives. Recommend a non-5xx status (e.g. 409/422) or 200 with {success:false, detail:...} so the German message survives the edge.

Emergent email proxy returns 429 'email rate limit exceeded' on bursts (~5+ sends in quick succession), which the endpoint maps to a generic 502. Consider surfacing a distinct German message for rate-limit (429) vs. undeliverable (422) so admins know to retry rather than assuming a hard failure.

ui_bugs.issue: On a 502 from the reply endpoint the error box renders raw English Cloudflare text ('The origin web server returned an invalid or incomplete response to Cloudflare…') instead of the German fallback 'Versand fehlgeschlagen.' — non-JSON/HTML error bodies must be filtered before display.

issues: No blocking issues found. Timeline, contact card, reply form and Bearbeitung section render with adequate contrast and spacing; status badges legible.

action_items: Replace the 502 status for mail-provider failures with an edge-safe status (409/422) or 200+{success:false}, because Cloudflare swallows 5xx bodies and the German error text never reaches the admin UI.

Harden ReplyForm error handling: only display e.response.data.detail when it is a short JSON string; otherwise show 'Versand fehlgeschlagen.' (currently an English Cloudflare HTML message is shown to the admin).
Optional: differentiate provider 429 (rate limit → 'Bitte in einer Minute erneut versuchen') from 422 (undeliverable recipient) in the German error copy.
critical_code_review_comments: ReplyIn does not set model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid'); extra payload fields (email/to/recipient) are silently ignored (verified: mail still goes to the stored handoff.email). Behaviour is safe, but 'Pydantic strict' as claimed in the spec is not actually enabled — consider extra='forbid' to fail loudly.

reply_handoff/patch_handoff use read-then-update (find_one then find_one_and_update); concurrent replies could both see status 'new' and push two 'in_progress' history entries. Low risk for an admin inbox, but a single conditional update ({_id, status:'new'}) would be race-free.
The unused helper _apply_status_change() in assistant_admin.py is dead code (PATCH and reply both build their own update ops) — remove or use it to remove duplication.

AdminAssistantHandoffs.jsx (610 lines) mixes Timeline, ReplyForm, ReplySignal, DetailDrawer and the list page; splitting into components/admin/handoffs/* would keep files under the 700-line guideline as the page grows.
Initial inbox load is delayed by the 350 ms debounce timer (the same effect handles mount + search); acceptable, but an immediate first fetch would remove the visible 'Wird geladen…' latency.

flaky_tests: TestReplySuccess::test_recipient_manipulation_ignored and test_html_injection_escaped_and_stored — ~33% failure rate purely from the Emergent email proxy 429 burst limit; both pass when re-run after a short pause (env limitation, not an app bug).
rca_of_the_issue: The reply endpoint correctly raises HTTPException(502) with a German detail and performs no DB mutation on mail failure (confirmed via origin curl: {'detail':'Mailversand ist fehlgeschlagen. Der Handoff wurde nicht verändert.'} + reply_count 0, status still 'new', empty reply_history/status_history). However the Cloudflare edge in front of the preview URL intercepts 5xx responses and substitutes its own 'Bad gateway' HTML page; axios therefore surfaces that English text and the admin sees infra wording instead of the intended German message. Fix at the status-code level (non-5xx) and defensively in the ReplyForm catch block.
